acceptance: `make pr-open PR_BASE=<parent>` opens a draft PR against the parent branch
The conflict check and existing-PR lookup use the parent, not develop
Without PR_BASE the behaviour is unchanged
A unit test covers both paths
context: Add an option such as `PR_BASE=<branch>` that opens a draft against that branch and runs the same checks against the parent instead of `develop`. Reject a parent that is not an open PR's head branch. `tests/unit/workflows/test_stacked_pr_base_guard.py` covers the CI side of the policy.
description:
`docs/internal/pr-base-branch-policy.md` says a PR stacked on another open PR must be a draft that targets its parent's branch. The `pr-open` recipe in the root `Makefile` always targets `develop`: it fetches `origin/develop`, checks for conflicts against it, and looks up existing PRs with `--base develop`. It has no base or draft option.

So the stacked case has to be done by hand with `gh pr create --draft --base <parent>`. That skips the recipe's preflight, conflict scan and trunk-revert gate.
